summary: Several added comments contradict edge-case behavior or omit material failures inherited from the implementations they override.

items.issue: `ofUnit` has no backing array, yet `resize` records a positive capacity after additions; therefore capacity is not always 0 while no backing array is allocated.
items.suggestion: Qualify the description as applying to array-backed builders, and describe the `ofUnit` exception if documenting the shared field.

items.issue: The shared implementation also serves `ofUnit`, whose `resize` only records capacity and allocates no backing array. The summary incorrectly says it grows a backing array.
items.suggestion: Say it ensures capacity, and qualify backing-array allocation as behavior of array-backed implementations.

items.issue: `ofUnit` inherits this method but has no backing array to grow; its override of `resize` only updates `capacity`.
items.suggestion: Describe reserving/recording capacity generally, with allocation limited to array-backed builders.

items.issue: The documented `IllegalStateException` condition is false when `xs.knownSize` is 0: the method neither iterates `xs` nor verifies that it yields zero elements, so a mismatching iterator does not throw.
items.suggestion: Narrow the exception condition to a positive reported known size, or change the implementation to validate zero-size reports too.

items.issue: NEEDS-HUMAN: Is the override intentionally allowed to ignore `xs` and `offset`, accept a negative `length`, and inflate its count beyond the supplied slice? This differs from the base overload’s clamped-slice contract.
items.suggestion: Resolve the intended contract before merge; then either repair the override to honor the base slice semantics or retain and document the deliberate divergence without the NEEDS-HUMAN marker.

items.issue: The public constructor omits its material failure case: `ArrayDeque.alloc` throws `IllegalArgumentException` for a negative or unrepresentably large initial size.
items.suggestion: Add an `@throws IllegalArgumentException` tag describing invalid initial-size hints.

items.issue: The claimed O(min(idx, length - idx)) time excludes a full-buffer insertion: `mustGrow` then allocates and copies all existing elements, which is O(length), including at either endpoint.
items.suggestion: Qualify the bound as excluding a resize, or document the amortized/resize cost accurately.

items.issue: It does not resize at most once for every input. At `idx == length`, it delegates to `addAll`; for an unknown-size source, that appends one element at a time and can resize repeatedly.
items.suggestion: Limit the one-resize claim to known-size sources or revise the implementation.

items.issue: The documentation presents `end` as any number of leading elements, but construction calls `reset`, which requires `0 <= end < array.length`; `end == array.length` cannot represent a full deque because one circular-buffer slot remains unused.
items.suggestion: Document the valid `end` range and resulting exception, and apply the same correction to `ArrayDequeOps.ofArray`.

items.issue: A negative `destStart` is not a no-op: when there are elements to copy, `copySliceToArray` calls `requireBounds` and throws `IndexOutOfBoundsException`. The comment omits this material case.
items.suggestion: Add an `@throws IndexOutOfBoundsException` tag for a negative destination start.

items.issue: The override delegates to `IndexedSeqOps.sliding`, whose returned iterator throws `java.util.ConcurrentModificationException` if this sequence’s length changes during iteration. The new documentation omits that material exception.

`grouped` delegates to this `sliding(n, n)` implementation, so its returned iterator likewise throws `java.util.ConcurrentModificationException` if the collection length changes during iteration; the documentation omits it.
items.suggestion: Add the inherited concurrent-modification failure case to the documentation.
